title: Linear and Quadratic Inequalities
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Linear and Quadratic Inequalities. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Order and transformations

An inequality compares values using (\(<\)), (le), (\(>\)), or (ge). Adding or subtracting the same quantity preserves its direction. Multiplication or division by a positive number also preserves it; multiplication or division by a negative number reverses it.

Solution sets

A solution is any value that makes the original inequality true. Show a strict endpoint with an open circle and an inclusive endpoint with a closed circle. A compound inequality can describe an interval, such as (\(2 \le x < 7\)).

Polynomial inequalities

For a factored product, mark its zeros on a number line and test the sign in each interval. Include a zero only for a non-strict inequality. This sign-chart method also works for rational expressions after recording excluded denominator zeros.

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• Reverse the sign only when multiplying or dividing by a negative number.
  • Keep all three parts of a compound inequality in the same operation.
  • For products, use critical points and one test value per interval.
  • For rational inequalities, a denominator zero is excluded even if cancellation seems possible.
  • Substitute an interior value and check boundary inclusion separately.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• (\(a
  • For (\(x^2-a^2>0\)), the solution is (\(x<-a\)) or (\(x>a\)) when (\(a>0\)).
  • Interval brackets include endpoints; parentheses exclude them.
  • Multiplying by an expression of unknown sign requires a sign analysis.

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    Solve (\(3x-5<7\)).

    1. (\(x<4\))
    2. (\(x>4\))
    3. (\(x<2/3\))
    4. (\(x>2/3\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(x<4\))

    Add 5 to obtain (\(3x<12\)). Divide by positive 3: (\(x<4\)).

  2. Core:

    Solve (\(-2x+6\ge0\)).

    1. (\(x\ge3\))
    2. (\(x\le3\))
    3. (\(x\ge-3\))
    4. (\(x\le-3\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(x\le3\))

    (\(-2x\ge-6\)). Dividing by (\(-2\)) reverses the sign, giving (\(x\le3\)).

  3. Foundation:

    Solve (\(5x-4 \le 11\)).

    1. (\(x \le 3\))
    2. (\(x \ge 3\))
    3. (\(x \le 15/5\))
    4. (\(x \ge 15/5\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(x \le 3\))

    Add 4: (\(5x \le 15\)). Divide by positive 5: (\(x \le 3\)).

  4. Standard:

    Solve (\(-2x+6>0\)).

    1. (\(x>3\))
    2. (\(x<3\))
    3. (\(x>-3\))
    4. (\(x<-3\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(x<3\))

    Subtract 6: (\(-2x>-6\)). Dividing by (\(-2\)) reverses the sign, so (\(x<3\)).

  5. Challenge:

    Solve (\((x-2)(x+1) \le 0\)).

    1. (\(x \le -1 or x \ge 2\))
    2. (\(-1 \le x \le 2\))
    3. (\(x<-1\))
    4. (\(x>2\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(-1 \le x \le 2\))

    The zeros are (\(-1\)) and 2. The product is negative between the roots and zero at each endpoint, so (\(-1 \le x \le 2\)).
